meta.note: A thin day. The two-day window overlaps with yesterday, and most of its strongest pieces already ran on 2 October (Doherty's threshold, Luke Wroblewski on design systems, Vauxhall, PENNY, Shopify Canvas, the Graphite study on AI writing tells) or earlier this week (the Formula E identity). They are not repeated. The rest was gadget reviews, deals, data-centre politics and agency press releases. werbewoche.ch failed, the State of Brand sitemap had no page in the window, two paid Substack posts were removed before curation.

stories.title: In/Tension Modeling: check each solution against the people it might harm
stories.blurb: Part two of a UX research method: put conflicting voices from research side by side, reframe the tension as an opportunity, brainstorm against it, then use a Range of Tolerance tool to see where each affected group lands. The yardstick is Erika Hall's question of what gives designers the right to intervene on others' behalf.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: In/tension modeling: what gives us the right?

stories.title: identi leaves the category's greens and yellows behind
stories.blurb: Perfect Storm shortened identibase to identi and set one filter for every decision: the brand serves all of pet life, chaos included. That meant a bolder palette than the category's natural greens and yellows, less idealised photography with owners at eye level with their pets, and a warm voice that does not pretend to be a dog.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Perfect Storm helps switch pet protection firm from identibase to identi

stories.title: Jon Cook leaves WPP, Eric Campbell takes over VML
stories.blurb: Cook formed VML from VMLY&R and Wunderman Thompson in 2024 and since February has also run WPP Creative, the unit holding Ogilvy, Grey, AKQA, Landor and Design Bridge & Partners. He stays until March 2027; his long-time partner Eric Campbell succeeds him as VML CEO.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Jon Cook to leave WPP and transition VML CEO role to long-time partner Eric Campbell

stories.title: BRXND: once agents do the buying, brand is the hedge
stories.blurb: Mike Mallazzo argues that advertising is a bigger share of the economy than ever while the old model, The Trade Desk and the holding companies among it, wobbles. His conclusion for marketers: making product feeds legible to agents is not enough, the safer bet is a brand people tell their agent to buy by name.

sources.name: BRXND Dispatch
sources.headline: The Golden Age of Marketing // BRXND Dispatch vol. 142
